source: National Archives Bill of Rights transcript, Amendment III
review_notes: Codex reviewed the full Third Amendment. It states a peace-time prohibition without owner consent and a war-time requirement that quartering follow a manner prescribed by law. The source does not assert that anyone was quartered or that consent was given. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
Amendment III

No Soldier shall, in time of peace be quartered in any house, without the consent of the Owner, nor in time of war, but in a manner to be prescribed by law.
